subject: Skyline Health — benchmark engagement: dataset spec, scoring, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@skylinehealth.com>, Dr. Samir Shah <samir.shah@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Skyline Health — benchmark engagement: dataset spec, scoring, next steps

Hi Elena / Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the pilot: 

Key goals we heard:
- Automated triage of patient intake notes (classify urgency + route to specialty).
- Minimize hallucination on medication and diagnosis extraction (high precision required).
- Keep per-call latency under 350ms 95th percentile for the 4k-token workflow.

Recommended baseline models for the benchmark run:
- Mistral-7B-instruct (instruction-tuned) — fast, good for throughput testing.
- Llama2-13B-chat (standard) — better context handling, expected higher accuracy on complex prompts.
- Quantized 13B variant (int8) for cost/perf tradeoff testing.

What we need from you to run the initial customer-specific eval on Redwood:
1) Dataset (initial slice): CSV with columns [id, prompt, reference, metadata]; sample attached (skyline_sample_200.csv). Please aim for ~2k rows for the first run.
2) A short spec for what counts as a correct answer (labeling rules) and any critical PHI redaction rules.
3) Priority scoring metrics: accuracy (strict match), partial-match F1 for entities, hallucination rate (binary flag), latency targets. We'll provide scorer code that computes these.

Format & delivery notes:
- CSV layout we prefer: id, prompt, reference, notes, source_date, contains_phi (yes/no). See attached skyline_benchmark_template.csv.
- For prompts that require structured output, include an example expected JSON in the reference column.
- If you cannot share PHI, we can run inside your VPC/private deployment; let us know your preference.

Attachments: skyline_benchmark_template.csv, prompt_set_skyline_v1.jsonl, redwood_eval_instructions.pdf
Links: benchmark template (https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/skyline-benchmark-template)

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
- Elena: confirm whether PHI will be shared or if we should set up a Private run (you said you'd check with security). Deadline: Tue 2027-04-12.
- Skyline: share initial dataset sample (<= 200 rows) by Tue 2027-04-13.
- Redwood (Ben & Vivek): scope quantization and scoring parameters, provide scorer script and runbook by Wed 2027-04-14.

I'll compile answers and schedule a short 30-min follow-up next week to kick off the run. Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@skylinehealth.com>, Dr. Samir Shah <samir.shah@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Skyline Health — benchmark engagement: dataset spec, scoring, next steps

Marissa — adding technical clarifications so the customer has a concrete ask for the CSV and so engineering can prepare: 

- Tokenization/length: please note we will run tokenization with the tokenizer matching each model; for the initial pass assume max_input_tokens=4096 and max_output_tokens=512. If you have longer notes we'll need to truncate or use a sliding-window strategy.
- Sampling: we recommend running deterministic (greedy) and one temperature sweep (0.2, 0.7) to observe robustness. Include the sampling settings as columns in the CSV when applicable.
- Scoring script: we'll provide a scorer (redwood-eval-scorer-v1.py) that computes strict_match, entity_f1, hallucination_flag, and latency percentiles. We'll also include a small harness to run the scorer locally if you want. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/redwood-eval-scorer-v1.py
- Output format: where the reference is structured JSON, scorer will compare by key. We prefer references normalized to lowercase and whitespace-trimmed for strict_match.

I'll prep the scorer and a short containerized job to run this in either our hosted env or in your VPC.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Skyline Health — benchmark engagement: dataset spec, scoring, next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- PHI: we cannot share identifiable PHI to a hosted environment. We will either provide a de-identified slice or request a Private run inside our VPC. I'll confirm which by EOD Tue (2027-04-13).
- Timeline: we can deliver a 200-row sample by Tue 2027-04-13 and aim for the full ~2k sample by Fri 2027-04-23 (assuming legal approval).
- Question: can Redwood run the scorer and the model runs inside our Azure VNet? If so, what data transfer/ingest mechanisms do you support?

Attached: skyline_sample_200.csv (sample with synthetic notes).

Thanks team — Laura here. Approved next steps from a commercial/ops perspective: 

- Offer Skyline a one-week Dedicated pilot credit to run the initial benchmark inside a private project (cover compute costs up to $5k). This will help remove friction around PHI while we sort the legal addendum.
- Security: please loop in our Security & Legal on the VPC onboarding checklist; give me the timeline and I'll escalate if needed.
- I'll approve sharing the SOC2 summary and our KMS/HSM options with Elena.

Marissa/Ben: confirm the wording for the pilot credit and I will sign off on the MSA addendum draft.

Laura Bennett

Elena — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. Finalizing owners and dates below so there’s a clear action list: 

Owners & next steps:
- Elena (Skyline): confirm PHI approach (de-identified vs VPC) by EOD Tue 2027-04-13. (deliverable: reply to this thread)
- Elena: upload skyline_sample_200.csv to the Drive link or send via secure SFTP if preferred (we received the sample stub but please use secure channel for the real data). Target: 2027-04-13.
- Ben & Vivek (Redwood): deliver scorer script, container image, and quantization config; provide instructions for running inside Azure VNet by 2027-04-14.
- Laura (Redwood Ops): confirm pilot credit wording & MSA addendum owner by 2027-04-13.
- Marissa: schedule 30-min technical kickoff for Thu 2027-04-15 (invitation to follow).

If you prefer Redwood to run the benchmark inside your Azure VNet, Ben can share the onboarding checklist (network ports, service account, KMS keys). Otherwise we’ll stage the run in a private Redwood project with encryption at rest and in transit.

Thanks — I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu.

Best,
Marissa
